Bayesian variable selection for the HELIX pregnancy exposome and the
birth-weight z-score using an **Automatic Relevance Determination** (ARD)
prior: each coefficient has its own precision `alpha_j`, so irrelevant
exposures are shrunk towards zero.

Source: `EnvBRAN/vs_bayesian.ipynb`. The model `linear_regression_ard`
is in `src/models.jl`.

```{julia}
using ExposomicsJulia
using Turing, ReverseDiff, LinearAlgebra, Statistics, DataFrames
```

### Data

Maternal covariates (BMI, weight gain, age) and the 57 pregnancy exposures
of the clean HELIX dataset.

```{julia}
df  = load_helix_clean();
sel = vcat(HELIX_COVARIATES, helix_exposure_names(df))
Xdt = Matrix{Float64}(df[:, sel])
Ydt = Array{Float64}(df.bw_zscore);
```

### Automatic Relevance Determination linear Bayesian regression

```{julia}
m = linear_regression_ard(Xdt, Ydt)
```

```{julia}
#| eval: false
reg_ard = sample(m, NUTS(; adtype = AutoReverseDiff(; compile = true)), 1000);
```

```{julia}
#| eval: false
coeffs = chain_summary(reg_ard; quantiles = [0.025, 0.1, 0.5, 0.9, 0.975], pattern = "coefficients")
coeffs.parameter = sel
coeffs[coeffs.nonzero, :]
```
